ProjectQr__Description: Project QR Code: one QR symbol per project, carrying a short address that opens the project's live TrueVision model, printed automatically on every document in the pack so anybody holding a drawing can scan straight into 3D. The symbol is the same on every sheet of a project and different for every project. Every value here is a built-in default mirrored in Na__ProjectQr__Symbol__.js, so a failed fetch degrades to a working code rather than a missing one. WHERE a document puts the code is that document's business: the drawing title block's cell is sized in Na__LayoutEditor__AppConfig__.json under LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config (QrCell...).
ProjectQr__EnabledNote: False draws no code anywhere: every document asks this system for the symbol and draws nothing when it is given none. The title block then gives the cell's room back to the fields.

ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__Description: The address a scanned code opens. A PRINTED CODE OUTLIVES EVERYTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY - it sits in a site bag or a planning file for years - so whatever form is printed has to go on being answered for good.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__BaseUrlNote: THE RESOLVER, NOT THE APP, AND ALWAYS THE LIVE SITE. /q/ at the website root is a flat page (q/index.html) that looks the project code up in q/index.json and sends the phone on to the project's full TrueVision address. It is never window.location: drawings are authored and exported on localhost (the editor is read-only on the web), and a code reading http://localhost:8090/... opens on the authoring machine and on no phone in the world. THE FOLDER IS ONE LETTER ON PURPOSE - see LengthNote - and it must never be moved, renamed or removed.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__QueryPatternNote: Tokens: projectCode, projectFolder, year - read off the address bar by the same functions the project loader uses, and each URL-encoded. A token the pattern asks for that the project cannot supply draws NO code, because a code that scans to a broken address is worse than none. The bare code is the whole query: no key, no equals sign. If this pattern is ever changed, q/index.html must go on answering the old form, because it is already on paper.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__LengthNote: WHY THE ADDRESS IS THIS SHORT. Encoded length is the only thing deciding how many modules the symbol has, and module count against printed size is the only thing deciding whether a phone reads it. https://www.noble-architecture.com/q/?PS01 is 42 bytes, which is EXACTLY what a version 3 symbol holds at error correction M: 29 modules across. The project's full TrueVision address (.../na-apps/30__TrueVision__CoreAppCode/Index.html?project=PS01&project-folder=PS01__MustersRoad&year=26) is 135 bytes: version 8, 49 modules - in the 10 mm title block that is a 0.19 mm module, which no phone reads, and it took a 20 mm title block to print it at 0.35. Adam, 20-Sep-2026: 'too tall, too portrait-feeling, and stretched... could we have a top-level, root-level index to handle diverting these?' THERE IS NO HEADROOM: one more character anywhere - a longer folder name than q, a query key, a five character project code - is a version 4 symbol, 33 modules, and a module about a tenth smaller (0.270 mm for 0.303). The only lever left is the host: a short domain of its own (na3d.uk/PS01 is 20 bytes) would be version 2, 25 modules.
ProjectQr__Link__Config.ProjectQr__Link__IndexUrlNote: The resolver's index, relative to this system's folder, so it is found on the live site and on a local server rooted at the repository alike. It is written by na-apps/05__ProjectVision__CoreAppCode/ProjectVision__BuildScript__.py on every build, and --qr-index-only rewrites it alone. On the authoring machine this system reads it once per project and says so on the console if the project on screen is missing from it, or is listed under a different folder or year - because a drawing exported then would carry a code that opens nothing. Empty switches the check off, which is right only if BaseUrl is pointed back at an address that needs no index.

ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__Description: How the symbol is drawn, wherever it is drawn. Always vector: one filled path on the screen sheet, in a PDF and in an HTML page, never a raster.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__DarkColourNote: Pure black, not the sheet's ink colour (#172b3a), on purpose. A mono laser prints a colour as a halftone screen, and at a third of a millimetre per module a screen's dots are a real fraction of the module: the edges a camera has to find come out ragged. Black prints solid on every printer. Beside the navy text of the title block the difference cannot be seen; to a phone in a site cabin it is the difference that matters.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__PortalDarkColourNote: The dark modules of a code a VECTOR carries (Shape__Qr), which is the parametric scrapbook's Project Portal block in both its forms - and only that. hsl(0, 0%, 35%). Adam, 21-Sep-2026: 'instead of them being absolute black, make them softer ... so that they don't look so stark on the page and they still scan fine', after retouching one to this grey in Photoshop and scanning it. The title block's code keeps DarkColour. WHY THE PORTAL MAY BE SOFTER WHEN THE TITLE BLOCK MAY NOT: DarkColourNote's halftone screen, but at the Portal's size. Its smallest code, 15 mm, prints a 0.52 mm module and 20 mm (as dropped) 0.69 mm, where the title block prints 0.30 - so a laser's screen dots are a far smaller fraction of each module. Against the white it is 90 per cent symbol contrast (ISO/IEC 15415 grade A starts at 70). Na__Test__ProjectQr__.test.mjs holds it to that floor and Na__Test__ProjectQr__Decode__.py reads every case back at this grey as well as at black. Painted at painting time, so a block already on a sheet takes a new value on its next repaint with nothing to rebuild.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__QuietZoneModulesNote: The clear light margin a document keeps round the symbol, in modules. The title block sizes its code FROM this - the square is the strip's height less this many modules above and below - so it is a layout value, not advice: 2 modules in the 10 mm strip is a 0.61 mm margin round an 8.79 mm code, which is Lantern Designer's 0.6 mm and 8.8 mm arrived at by rule rather than typed in. ISO/IEC 18004 asks for 4. Two is what Lantern Designer has printed since August 2026 (0.6 mm round a 0.267 mm module), which Adam reports scanning fine, and what this system was proved at (see MinModuleMmNote); 4 was tried first and made the title block's margins look, in Adam's words, in need of being 'considerably tighter'. A document that leaves less than this says so on the console. The HTML painter builds the ISO 4 into the symbol's own viewBox, because a web page has the room.
ProjectQr__Symbol__Config.ProjectQr__Symbol__MinModuleMmNote: The smallest printed module a document should give the symbol, in millimetres. A document that draws the symbol smaller is told so on the console, once, with the size it would need - so a title block made lower, or an address made longer, cannot quietly take the code below what a phone can read. WHERE 0.28 COMES FROM: the shipped title block prints a version 3 symbol at 0.303 mm, and Lantern Designer's 33 module symbol prints at 0.267 mm in the same 8.8 mm square, which Adam reports 'working okay in the end'. The floor sits between the two, so the shipped drawing passes and the first thing to make it worse - a fifth character in a project code, which is version 4 and 0.270 mm in this strip - is reported. HOW IT WAS PROVED is in README__ProjectQrCode__.md: real exported PDFs rasterised by PyMuPDF and read by OpenCV, a far fussier reader than a phone, with not one wrong read. 80__Testing__PrototypeEnvironment/Na__Test__ProjectQr__.test.mjs holds this file to these numbers on every run.

ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__Description: The words that go with the code, so every document in the pack says the same thing beside it. {document} is what the reader is holding: a drawing sheet passes nothing and gets DefaultDocumentNoun, the Drawing Register and the Project Specification pass their own.
ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__HeadingTextNote: Adam, 20-Sep-2026: 'Navigate' for 'View' - it sounds better, and it is what the reader is being offered: a model to walk round, not a picture to look at.
ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__BodyText: Scan this {document} to enter the 3D model and view the building in full 3D, and to freely navigate and take a tour.
ProjectQr__Note__Config.ProjectQr__Note__CompactTextNote: All there is room for where a document can spare the code a caption and no more. A drawing on A4 turns it up the code's left side, where the whole note would have cut the fields of the title block short. It has the code's own 8.8 mm to run along, which is eight capitals and not a sentence.
